headline: Journalists' group condemns State Minister Humayun Kabir over citizenship row
summary: The Bangladeshi Journalists in International Media (BJIM) called for an apology after the minister dodged questions about his British citizenship.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir faced backlash after reacting aggressively to journalists' questions regarding his British citizenship. During a briefing at the Foreign Ministry, he avoided giving a direct answer and instead questioned the motives of the reporters.

The controversy stems from reports questioning whether Kabir renounced his British citizenship to meet constitutional requirements before joining the cabinet. Kabir previously served as a councillor for Bensham Manor and was the Mayor of Croydon from 2019 to 2020 in the UK.

The Bangladeshi Journalists in International Media (BJIM) issued a statement describing the minister's response as 'unprofessional and aggressive.' They argued that his behavior was an attempt to intimidate the media and discourage accountability.
BJIM has called on State Minister Humayun Kabir to withdraw his remarks and provide a clear, specific answer regarding his citizenship status and constitutional eligibility to hold office.

The journalists' group emphasized that reporters are not adversaries but perform a vital public service by asking questions on behalf of citizens. They urged the government to ensure a fear-free environment for the press.

headline: Chittagong: Depositors protest as bank blocks savings withdrawals
summary: Around 150 customers of First Security Islami Bank gathered at the zonal office in Halishahar to demand access to their money, citing urgent medical needs.
details: Around 100 to 150 depositors gathered at the First Security Islami Bank zonal office in Halishahar, Chittagong, to protest the blocking of their savings withdrawals.
One protester, Md. Alauddin, shared a heartbreaking account of being unable to afford his mother's medical treatment despite having funds in the bank.

The Combined Islamic Bank Victim Depositors Association (Chittagong Committee) led the protest, claiming that customers across various branches have faced non-cooperation when trying to withdraw money.
Association leaders stated they had visited several branches over the last 15 days to document the widespread issues depositors are facing.
Following discussions with zonal office authorities, the association reported that the problems of approximately 66 depositors were resolved immediately.
Other urgent applications were reportedly prioritized and sent to the head office for swift settlement.
The protest was led by association president Md. Abul Kalam Azad, general secretary Jahangir Hossain, and other committee members.
Depositors from areas including Keranihat, Maheshkhali, Patiya, and Anwara participated in the demonstration to demand normal banking services.
